text:
alex: Heads-up — saw 5 incidents today where downstream services lost tracing because our rewrite rules strip X-Request-ID. Can we revisit ordering and precedence?
maria: ugh, that explains the missing traces :grimacing: which rule is stripping it?
alex: the 'normalize-headers' transform runs after 'kv-cache' canonicalization. It removes all headers not in allowlist, and our allowlist didn't have X-Request-ID. PR #612 added it but only to canary; main route still missing.
tim: can you paste the problematic rule?
alex: sure — snippet from gateway config:```yaml- route: /v1/generate*  transform_order: [path_normalize, query_rewrite, header_cleanup, inject_canary]  header_cleanup: allowlist: [Accept, Authorization, Content-Type]  inject_canary: add: {x-canary: canary-42}```
maria: couple concerns: 1) path_normalize currently collapses duplicate slashes and strips trailing slash — that breaks some customer routes that treat "/v1/foo" vs "/v1/foo/" differently. 2) inject_canary runs last so it overwrites existing x-canary that some SDK sets.
srini: Maybe we need a header precedence enum on transforms: preserve_existing | override | append. Right now transforms assume override.
alex: Agreed. Also query_rewrite currently runs before header_cleanup, so clients sending tracking params get them removed later. That ordering is surprising. I'd expect header_cleanup first (to prune sensitive tokens), then query_rewrite, then path_normalize?
maria: For path trailing-slash: we could make normalization opt-in per-route with mode: preserve|strip|redirect. Redirect would return 301 to canonical path which keeps semantics.
tim: Redirects might increase latency for sync calls though. For internal routes we can canonicalize, for customer-facing keep preserve. Can we add a config example?
srini: propose per-route config:```json
{"path_norm":{"mode":"preserve","collapse_double_slashes":true},"header_cleanup":{"allowlist":["Accept","Content-Type","X-Request-ID"],"precedence":"preserve_existing"},"inject_canary":{"add":{"x-canary":"canary-42"},"precedence":"append"}}
```
alex: That looks good. Precedence options should also be exposed in Console UI with a tooltip: "preserve_existing — don't overwrite headers the client sent"
maria: Also request we add a tiny telemetry event when a rewrite changes a header/query/path: {route, transform, before, after} — low-sample rate. Otherwise debugging is painful.
deploy-bot: deploy started for gateway-schema v2.18.5 on prod (canary 10%)
tim: one more edge: caching key currently computed before query_rewrite. So normalized queries aren't used in cache key causing cache misses. We should compute cache key after normalization/rewrites.
srini: yeah reorder: header_cleanup -> path_normalize -> query_rewrite -> compute_cache_key -> inject_canary. We'll need to record transform timings in telemetry.
maria: can someone file a tiny RFC / ops-runbook? I can draft the runbook for rollback and how to audit live routes.
alex: I'll open RFC and add example migration steps and a small test harness to fuzz header precedence. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
